text:
oliver: Heads-up — during the overnight e2e runs CA wound up provisioning 12 GPU spot nodes in eu-west-1, then we had a sudden scale-down churn and ~30 pods got rescheduled. Latency for the inference path spiked ~400ms. 

maya: ugh. do we have the autoscaler logs? was it choosing the cheapest group or packing? :eyes:

oliver: grabbed the CA snippet — looks like it used the default expander behavior (most-pods) and picked the spot pool that fit more pods. after startup the cloud provider reclaimed several spot instances and we saw mass evictions. log excerpt:

```
I0314 03:12:14.123456   12345 scale_up.go:299] Best option: nodegroup gpu-spot-1. Reason: most pods fit (waste 2)
I0314 03:12:50.987654   12345 cloudprovider.go:512] Instance terminated by provider: spot instance interruption
I0314 03:13:04.234567   12345 scale_down.go:210] Removing node: gpu-spot-1-xyz (utilization 0.12)
```

samir: that matches the cost tradeoff we saw in feb. mixing spot + on-demand without weights tends to cause oscillation when spot flaps. can we avoid CA preferring spot for stable critical workloads? :thinking: 

lina: two quick knobs we should consider: prefer `--expander=least-waste` (reduces fragmentation) or switch to `--expander=most-pods` + node-group priority annotations if we want to keep behavior but weight on-demand higher. also tune scale-down timings and max provisioning time.

samir: my recommendation (small changes first):
- set `--expander=least-waste`
- enable `--balance-similar-node-groups`
- increase `--max-node-provision-time=15m`
- `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m` (was 5m)
- `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5`
- `--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m`

oliver: sounds reasonable. can we also enforce a min=1 for the on-demand gpu nodegroup so we never scale it to zero? keep spot as bursty buffer.

lina: yes — set nodegroup min size to 1 for `gpu-on-demand-eu` and keep `gpu-spot-eu` min 0. also annotate model-serving pods with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false"` for the few latency-sensitive pods so CA doesn't kick them out during scale-down decisions.

maya: quick config example for CA flags (proposal):

```
--expander=least-waste \
--balance-similar-node-groups \
--max-node-provision-time=15m \
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m \
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5 \
--scale-down-delay-after-add=15m
```

plus: set `minSize: 1` on `gpu-on-demand-eu` ASG. and add a tiny dedicated pool (min 1 / max 2) for critical model-serving to avoid cold-starts.

samir: I want us to also emit a metric for CA decision reasons (which nodegroup it picked + expander reason) so we can query how often spot vs on-demand is chosen and correlate with provider interruptions. can someone add a Grafana dashboard?

oliver: putting a Grafana card on the infra dashboard. i'll also open a PR for the CA flag change and the nodegroup min-size change. tagging @lina for the pod annotation changes.

infra-bot: Created PR #821: "autoscaler: prefer least-waste, balance nodegroups, tune scale-down" — https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pull/821 :github: 

maya: nice. after PR lands let's run canary e2e on staging for 24h and check restart/eviction counts and p95 latency before flipping prod. :thumbsup:

lina: agreed. I'll prepare the pod annotation patch and a short runbook for on-call if scale churn recurs.

oliver: thanks all. action items: PR by oliver, pod annotation + runbook by lina, Grafana by samir, staging canary test by maya. will follow up tomorrow with results. :white_check_mark:
